questions.q: LASER stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of ___.
questions.exp: The expansion given is Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. (Book p228)

questions.q: Match the laser effect with the tissue result — 1) Photoablation  2) Photodisruption  3) Photocoagulation … A) Coagulate  B) Break  C) Burn/vaporize
questions.exp: The overview classifies photoablation as burning tissue, photodisruption as breaking tissue and photocoagulation as coagulating tissue. (Book p228)

questions.q: Photoablation acts by breaking chemical bonds and vaporizing tissue; it uses which wavelength range?
questions.exp: Photoablation produces chemical effects, breaks bonds and vaporizes tissue; the listed wavelength is ultraviolet 150-300 nm. (Book p228)

questions.q: Which laser and procedures are paired correctly for corneal refractive surgery?
opts: Diode, 810 nm; posterior capsulotomy and iridotomy
Argon-fluoride excimer, 193 nm; LASIK and PRK
questions.exp: The excimer argon-fluoride laser is listed at 193 nm; photoablation applications include LASIK and PRK. (Book p228)

questions.q: Photocoagulation produces a thermal effect that causes:
questions.exp: Photocoagulation's mechanism is thermal denaturation of proteins; its listed wavelength is visible spectrum 400-580 nm. (Book p228)

questions.q: Which list correctly matches photocoagulation laser with wavelength?
opts: Argon green 514 nm; frequency-doubled Nd:YAG 532 nm; diode 810 nm; ruby red 694 nm
Argon 193 nm; Nd:YAG 694 nm; diode 532 nm; ruby 810 nm
Argon 1064 nm; Nd:YAG 810 nm; diode 694 nm; ruby 532 nm
Argon 400 nm; Nd:YAG 580 nm; diode 193 nm; ruby 1053 nm
questions.exp: The photocoagulation examples are argon green 514 nm, frequency-doubled Nd:YAG 532 nm, diode 810 nm (preferred for ROP) and ruby red 694 nm. (Book p228)

questions.q: Panretinal photocoagulation is listed for diabetic retinopathy and CRVO; laser trabeculoplasty is used for:
questions.exp: Photocoagulation uses include PRP for diabetic retinopathy/CRVO and trabeculoplasty for POAG. (Book p228)

questions.q: Focal retinal photocoagulation is listed for diabetic macular edema, CSR and:
questions.exp: Focal retinal laser uses listed are diabetic macular edema, CSR and ARMD. (Book p228)

opts: Ultraviolet bond breaking followed by vaporization
Ionization, plasma-mediated bond breakage and acoustic shock waves
questions.exp: Photodisruption combines electron stripping/ionization, plasma-like material that breaks bonds and acoustic shock waves producing mechanical effect. (Book p228)

questions.q: The invisible photodisruption beam is aimed using a visible ___ beam.
questions.exp: Infrared photodisruption is invisible; a helium-neon red beam is used to view and aim. (Book p228)

questions.q: Which photodisruption laser wavelengths are listed?
questions.exp: The photodisruption table lists Nd:YAG 1064 nm and Nd:glass 1053 nm. (Book p228)

questions.q: Nd:glass is listed for FLACS and:
questions.exp: Nd:glass uses include FLACS for cataract surgery and SMILE for refractive-error correction. (Book p228)

questions.q: Nd:YAG photodisruption is used for posterior capsulotomy for PCO and peripheral iridotomy for:
questions.exp: Nd:YAG is listed for posterior capsulotomy in PCO and peripheral iridotomy in angle-closure glaucoma. (Book p228)

units.title: Laser principles and tissue effects
units.guide: LASER means Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. Classify ocular laser effects as photoablation (burn/vaporize), photodisruption (break) or photocoagulation (coagulate), then connect mechanisms, wavelengths, devices and clinical uses.
